prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands at magic angles in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in moire graphene

statement.case_for: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene is the clearest recent case of theory leading experiment in condensed matter. The 2011 Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted that a twist angle quenches the kinetic energy, and the 2018 experiments of Jarillo-Herrero's group then found correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle. A two-dimensional crystal that few expected to be interesting turned out to be a tunable platform with a new control knob, and the idea has spread to other van der Waals moire systems. It is reproducible: many independent groups have reproduced the phase diagram, and the continuum-model band structure is quantitatively checked against scanning-probe and transport data and against DFT-based tight-binding calculations. It also connects to the quantum-materials theme where quantum mechanics keeps producing surprises. The three-person theory-plus-experiment structure fits the prize rules without forcing an arbitrary cut.
statement.case_against: The microscopic origin of the superconductivity is unsettled, sample-to-sample variability is considerable, and the experimental team around Jarillo-Herrero (Cao, Fatemi and others) and earlier theory (Lopes dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto) make the attribution contestable with a limit of three names. A cautious committee could argue that the field is still moving fast and that the physics is not yet as settled as for the optical lattice clock or the topological insulators.

responses.point: Goran Johansson ranks B009 only fifth, judging it slightly early because the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is not settled, while placing optical lattice clocks (B049) first.
responses.response: I take the maturity point seriously, and I agree the pairing mechanism is open. But the discovery claim rests on the correlated insulator and the superconducting dome appearing at the predicted angle, which many groups have reproduced. The open mechanism question is the usual state of a young field, not a doubt about the discovery. I respect the clock case and would put B049 as my first alternative, but I find it the less surprising achievement: it is an extraordinary refinement of a known measurement principle rather than a new state of matter. I would not let the unsettled mechanism push the prize later.

responses.point: Stefan Kroll ranks optical lattice clocks first as a textbook measurement advance, confirmed by many independent laboratories and timely, and B009 is not on his ranked list.
responses.response: The independent confirmation of the clocks is exemplary, and I accept that the two-name attribution is cleaner than my three-name one. But I would ask what physical discovery stands at the centre: this is a metrology achievement whose main scientific consequences (tests of relativity, redefinition of the second) are still to come. I accept the attribution advantage of B049 and will not treat it as a weak case, but on the criterion of a verified new physical phenomenon I still favour B009.

responses.point: Eva Olsson ranks B009 first as the origin of the moire field, with a fair experiment-versus-theory split, but asks that the historical record on earlier flat-band theory and related experiments be checked.
responses.response: I agree with the split and share the caution on the record. Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto identified the reduced bandwidth at small angles before 2011, but the quantitative magic-angle condition with a precise flat-band mechanism is the Bistritzer-MacDonald result, and that is what the experiments tested. On the experimental side, the first author of the 2018 papers (Cao) is a real difficulty. I would keep the citation worded around the prediction and the discovery rather than around an individual, so that the attribution rests on the decisive contributions.

responses.point: Bernhard Mehlig places B009 fourth, calling it timely but possibly early on the superconductivity aspect, while the flat-band and correlated-insulator parts are secure.
responses.response: I agree with his own distinction, and it is why I would word the citation around flat bands and the correlated insulating and superconducting states as observed, not around a pairing mechanism. The secure part of the physics is enough for a prize. I would, however, ask whether the quantized-conductance concerns he raises for B026 are comparable in weight, since I consider B026 the next strongest condensed-matter candidate and I would value his view of whether it is the more mature choice.

responses.point: Ulf Danielsson ranks the IceCube astrophysical neutrino discovery (B047) first, as a discovery from nature that opened a new window, with Halzen as sole laureate, and ranks B009 second.
responses.response: I defer to him and others on astroparticle physics, and I accept that the diffuse flux is a real discovery that has been confirmed independently. My reservation is with attribution: a single name for a detector built by a large collaboration, with AMANDA, Baikal and DUMAND as predecessors, seems hard to defend, and source identification rests on a single blazar association. I think that makes B047 a candidate for later, while B009 has a more natural and fair trio now.

uncertainties: Whether the committee judges the superconducting mechanism still too open for a prize on magic-angle graphene now, or accepts the flat-band prediction plus correlated-state discovery as complete.
Whether the experimental credit should go to Jarillo-Herrero alone or include Cao and other members of his group, which the three-name limit makes difficult.
Whether the prior flat-band work of Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto changes the theoretical attribution.
I cannot independently judge the astroparticle and gamma-ray candidates and defer to colleagues on their maturity.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile: none of the credited candidates for B009, B049 or B026 is a known collaborator or institutional colleague of mine at Uppsala or Los Alamos, or in the DFT and atomistic spin dynamics community. My field proximity to condensed-matter theory is a source of expertise, not a personal connection.
